name: Keiko Ruiz
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember taking a holiday cake to a doorstep with no wreath.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Keiko by a small Wednesday habit. Keiko prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I have the recipe nobody else remembers. It calls for leaving one bun on a lonely neighbor's step.
appearance: Keiko has two white streaks in otherwise dark hair, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Keiko starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Keiko never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Keiko can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To leave a warm bun on a lonely doorstep.
family: Grey Good is Keiko’s half-sibling. Keiko chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Grey brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A wall of birthdays*, Grey says, “I papered over the wall because my boy never reached his next mark.”
connections: Layla Jimenez. A cook who can't smell can still follow a holiday gift to the right neighbor.

reactions.situation: A customer wants a bun saved until evening
reactions.response: Keiko writes the customer's name and collection time on the wrapped bun.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Keiko asks them privately what can be shared about the delay and respects the answer.

reactions.situation: When a relative hints at needing company
reactions.response: Keiko may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
